thread:
support-bot: New ticket CS-9321 created by Acme Corp — 
Customer: embeddings returned different vector lengths across deployments. Hosted -> 1536, Dedicated -> 768, Private unknown. Severity: high (customer-facing search break). Trace IDs attached.

morgan: pinging @jordan and @devon — customer says they call the same API path and model alias. They pasted a minimal repro: 

curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"embeddings-recommended","input":"who is the CEO of acme"}' | jq .

-> hosted result: { "data": [ { "embedding": [0.0001, 0.0023, ...] /* length 1536 */ ] } ] }

-> dedicated result: { "data": [ { "embedding": [0.0004, 0.0012, ...] /* length 768 */ ] } ] }

morgan: Customer insists they didn't change anything on their side. They tried same key in both envs. They also tried sending an array of 8 inputs and saw inconsistent lengths across responses in the same request.

jordan: noted — batching won't change embedding dimension. Most likely an alias/resolution issue where "embeddings-recommended" resolves to different underlying models per deploy. Can we confirm model routing for the tenant? Ask them to run `GET /v1/models` with the same key on hosted and on-prem. Also asking infra to dump routing table for their dedicated pool.

devon: pulling config now. Quick heads-up: we recently rolled an alias remap for a canary where `embeddings-recommended` -> `text-embedding-3-large` on Hosted, but on Dedicated the alias accidentally pointed to `text-embedding-2-small` in the cluster override. Repro of the misconfiguration:

--- deploy override snippet (dedicated cluster) ---
overrides:
  MODEL_ALIAS_OVERRIDES:
    embeddings-recommended: text-embedding-2-small
--- end ---

devon: that would explain exact 1536 vs 768 split. Changing alias changes vector size.

ivan: adding that runtime/batching or quantization can't flip vector length. If dimension differs it's definitely different model architecture. Also checked logs for trace `tr_7c9a` from the customer's request:

[2026-10-03T14:11:02Z] trace tr_7c9a tenant=acme route=embeddings-recommended resolved_model=text-embedding-3-large host=hosted-r1
[2026-10-03T14:11:05Z] trace tr_7c9a tenant=acme route=embeddings-recommended resolved_model=text-embedding-2-small host=dedicated-dc42

ivan: confirmed routing table mismatch.

morgan: ugh. Customer also worried about billing and whether this caused unexpected charges. If they were calling a smaller model in Dedicated, they'd be charged according to the model used (we bill per embedding unit + model multiplier). Need to confirm billing impact and whether we should credit.

devon: we should patch the Dedicated overrides to match Hosted, but we need to check why the override got applied. I see a PR from a week ago with a YAML that was intended for a different customer and mistakenly landed on the shared dedicated template. Will prepare rollback.

jordan: mitigation steps for customer: 1) Pin model explicitly in call to avoid alias resolution: "model": "text-embedding-3-large@v1". 2) Or set header `X-Redwood-Deployment: hosted` (if they want hosted). 3) We'll push an emergency config fix to dedicated.

morgan: shared commands for customer to pin — sending: 

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large@v1","input":["who is the CEO of acme"]}' | jq .

morgan: customer tried pinning and reported immediate parity with hosted — vector length 1536 returned.

acme-customer-rep: thanks, pinning fixed our immediate issue. Would like us to ensure alias parity across deployments and know what caused the misroute. Billing question: will we be refunded for the period we got the smaller model?

devon: replied — we'll calculate delta on the invoices based on model multipliers and visible usage. If we dropped their model to a cheaper one without notice we should credit the difference. I'll coordinate with finance.

sre-ops: pushed a hotfix to the dedicated cluster at 2026-10-03T15:04:12Z — removed unintended `MODEL_ALIAS_OVERRIDES` entry and reloaded routing. Patch: 

kubectl -n dedicated-prod set env deployment/embeddings-runtime MODEL_ALIAS_OVERRIDES='{}'
rolling restart deployment/embeddings-runtime

sre-ops: Post-fix verification: ran tenant-scope resolver for `acme` — both hosted and dedicated now resolve `embeddings-recommended` -> `text-embedding-3-large` and we see vector length 1536 in test calls.

morgan: verified with customer — they ran a batch of 8 texts and got 8 vectors of length 1536 from both Hosted and Dedicated. Customer confirmed search results restored.

ivan: notes for follow-up: add a test in the alias rollout job to diff resolved model IDs across deployment tiers; add an alert if alias resolves to different families (e.g., embeddings size mismatch). Also add a canary gate to prevent cross-tenant override leaks.

devon: I'll file a postmortem and tag infra/jenkins job that introduced wrong YAML. I'll also add a one-pager for support about pinning models and billing expectations.

morgan: closing loop with customer, ticket CS-9321 will be marked resolved once finance confirms any credits. Thanks all :party_parrot: 

support-bot: Ticket CS-9321 status: awaiting finance confirmation (owner: devon).
